Overview

pastey is a Claude Code plugin with one opening mechanism. When Claude writes a file (Write, Edit, MultiEdit), a PostToolUse hook runs the opener, which checks the path against allow/deny globs and launches the editor. Pasteable text that would otherwise exist only in chat reaches the same path through the skill, which has Claude save it as snippets/NNNN-name.<ext>; the hook then opens it like any other file.

Claude writes file ──▶ PostToolUse hook ──▶ pastey_open.py ──▶ editor CLI
Claude has copy/paste text ──▶ skill ──▶ writes snippets/NNNN-….ext ──▶ (same hook)

Design: pastey design spec.

Components

Matching and config (scripts/pastey_open.py, config/defaults.toml)

matches(rel, globs) implements **, * and ? globs anchored at the project root (case-insensitive on Windows). load_config merges config/defaults.toml, the user file (~/.pastey.toml, or $PASTEY_USER_CONFIG) and the project .pastey.toml: editor and editor_args override, allow and deny lists are additive. A malformed layer is skipped and reported through on_error.

Opener (scripts/pastey_open.py)

main() reads the hook JSON on stdin and calls handle(), which resolves the written path against $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (else the payload cwd), applies deny-then-allow, consults the per-session record (%TEMP%\pastey\session-<id>.json, atomic writes) and launches <editor> <editor_args> <path> detached. A Write whose tool_response.type is create always opens; other writes open once per session. main() always returns 0; errors go to %TEMP%\pastey\pastey.log. Set PASTEY_DEBUG=1 to log each raw payload. PASTEY_STATE_DIR and PASTEY_USER_CONFIG relocate the state directory and user config (used by the tests).

Three Windows-driven safeguards, each found by review and pinned by a test:

  • Hook stdin is read as bytes and decoded as UTF-8, not with the locale encoding, so non-ASCII paths arrive intact.
  • On Windows the editor resolves to code.cmd, which runs through cmd.exe. If the path to open contains any of & | < > ^ % ", launch refuses (ValueError, logged) rather than let a crafted filename execute commands.
  • Config layers are read as UTF-8 (a BOM is accepted) and type-checked: editor must be a string and editor_args, allow, deny lists of strings. A layer that fails to decode, parse or validate is skipped whole and logged; the other layers still apply.

Plugin wiring (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json)

The plugin is named pastey. hooks.json registers one PostToolUse hook on Write|Edit|MultiEdit that runs uv run --no-project ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pastey_open.py under bash. The script's PEP 723 header requires Python 3.11+, which uv provides.

Skill (skills/pastey/SKILL.md)

Instructions only, no code. It tells Claude when copy/paste text deserves a snippet file, how to pick the next 4-digit number from snippets/, how to name it (NNNN-what-it-does.<ext>, extension chosen for syntax highlighting), to use Write so the hook sees it, to never overwrite earlier snippets, and to say which file it wrote.
